question: did the timber re-tone change what the shipped viewer draws, and can this frame judge it
method: same page, same walk station, same camera, before and after the re-tone; the wall and floor act as a control because nothing about them changed
findings: The re-tone is live and behaves as designed: the controls are byte-identical, and the timber moves in exactly the channels the gain touches - red most, green a little, blue not at all (gain 2.34, 1.41, 0.98).

This frame cannot judge the timber colour. The door face in it sits at sRGB 15 against a wall at 160, a tenfold difference: it is the back of an open door turned into a dark corner, and almost nothing of what it shows is diffuse. A 2.34x lift in albedo moved it two levels.

So the black door in the pre-re-tone frame was shade, not albedo, and the re-tone should not be credited with fixing it. The re-tone stands on the hue measurement in build/timber-colour-r41.json alone - the delivery sat at red/blue 2.09 where both estimates of the photographs put it past 3.3 - and that basis is unaffected by any of this.
outstanding: a close view of one lit door face. The measurement above covers every wood_dark surface in the frame, doors among them, but does not frame a single leaf large enough to judge by eye.

lit_frame_attempt.why: the attic isometric shows door leaves in lit rooms, which walk mode at that station does not - it looks at the back of an open door in a dark corner
lit_frame_attempt.reading: the population of dark warm pixels nearly doubles, which is what warming the timber should do - surfaces too neutral to qualify before now qualify - while its mean barely moves because the pixels joining it are the marginal ones
lit_frame_attempt.caveat: this is not a clean A/B. The two frames came from different paths - the first clicked the floor button, the second opened on ?view=f3 - and 43310 pixels differ with peaks of over 100 levels in both directions, which is geometry shifting under a slightly different camera, not albedo.
lit_frame_attempt.conclusion: the re-tone is live and measurable, and it warms the timber; what a lit interior door face looks like after it is still unverified. The walk sweep that would have shown one did not finish under software rendering.

clean_ab.method: the pre-re-tone delivery extracted out of git and served through MODEL_ROOT, so both frames come down the identical code path with the identical camera; what differs between them is the build and nothing else, which means the changed pixels are the timber without having to guess at boxes
clean_ab.conclusion: the re-tone is real and proportionate in the shipped viewer. The dark interior timber - the doors - warms most, red over blue 1.27 to 1.60 and +27% red; the sunlit exterior timber, the fascia and shutters, warms modestly, 1.24 to 1.29, which was the risk worth checking and it did not turn orange.
